detail.longDescription: I spent weeks debugging a GA4 property that received zero traffic despite everything checkable looking correct: - gtag.js script loads fine (200 response) - window.dataLayer exists and fills up with the right-looking consent, js, and config commands - Google Tag Assistant finds the tag and correctly identifies its source as "On-page gtag('config')" - But Tag Assistant's "Hits Sent" tab always says "No hits were sent by this tag" - GA4 Realtime never shows a session, ever I ruled out: network/firewall blocking, every GA4 admin consent/collection toggle, a corrupted data stream (a brand new property + stream failed identically), duplicate tags, and CSP. Minimal reproducible example: function gtag(...args) { window.dataLayer.push(args); } window.dataLayer = []; window.gtag = gtag; gtag('config', 'G-XXXXXXXXXX'); // window.dataLayer now contains [ ['config', 'G-XXXXXXXXXX'] ] // which LOOKS correct, but this is a plain Array, not a real // JavaScript `arguments` object -- and gtag.js only recognizes // real `arguments` objects as commands. Every entry pushed this // way gets silently treated as inert data instead of being executed. What's the actual mechanism gtag.js uses to tell a real command apart from an ignored data-layer entry, and is there a way to prove this from the browser console before deploying any fix?
